ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit diagram, the upper horizontal wire is node a, respectively connected to the left branch, middle branch, and right branch. The left branch goes downward from a successively through R2 and voltage source E2; the middle branch goes downward from a through R3; the lower end of R3 and the lower end of E2 are connected by the lower wire. The right branch goes downward from a through voltage source E1 and resistor R1, and the lower end of R1 is grounded. Reasoning: According to the specified method, label the lower node shared by the lower end of R3 and the lower end of E2 as b. Let the current from a to b through the left branch be I2, and the current from a to b through R3 be I3; let the current of the right branch from a to ground be I1. Since node b is connected only to the two branches of the left branch and R3, using KCL at node b gives I2 + I3 = 0. Then using KCL at node a gives I1 + I2 + I3 = 0. Combining I2 + I3 = 0, one obtains I1 = 0. Therefore there is no current through R1 in the right branch, and thus no voltage drop. Thus the voltage of node a is determined only by the voltage source E1 in the right branch, Va = E1 = 6 V.
